summary: aitextkit-py ships obfuscated exec-on-import payload in a package advertised as simple text utilities
details: The package presents itself as a pure Python text-processing utility (functions such as clean_text, chunk_text, estimate_tokens, redact_secrets). However, both shipped source modules — src/aitextkit/text.py and src/aitextkit/system.py — contain no plaintext implementation of these functions. Instead, each file consists of a single obfuscated loader generated by pyobfuscator.com: `_ = lambda __: __import__('zlib').decompress(__import__('base64').b64decode(__[::-1])); exec((_)(b'...'))`. This reverses, base64-decodes, and zlib-decompresses an opaque byte string and passes the result to exec(). text.py is imported by the package's __init__.py, so this decode-and-exec chain runs on every `import aitextkit`. The advertised functionality is trivial text manipulation with no legitimate need for concealment; wrapping the entire library implementation in a decode+exec loader hides the actual runtime behavior from installers and reviewers, and executes arbitrary hidden code inside the importing Python process.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
